# Soul sheets: Saved replies (demo brand, 30 s promo, 16:9)

Brief: "A 30 second 16:9 promo for the demo brand announcing a new feature: saved replies for the support inbox. Five scenes. Voice-over in the brand voice."
Shared by all three: 16:9, 30 s cap (binding), voice-over by Justin (the only voice on the demo brand), confident energy (launch, not a sale), hook inside 3 s with the words on screen. Five scenes in the promo shape: hook, turn, proof, peak, close.
Brand voice: the demo brand has no written voice (`brand.md`, `rules.md` are empty on this). Used here: plain, warm, spoken to one support person. Said back so you can correct it.
Honest limit: the demo brand has no product (`brands/demo/product/` says so), so no real saved-replies screen exists to capture. See "Facts" and the storyboard note at the end.

---

## Concept A (recommended): "Again"

| | |
|---|---|
| Type | promo |
| Where it runs | Web, LinkedIn, in-product announcement |
| Size and length cap | 16:9, 30 s |
| Energy preset | confident (our recommendation: a launch to people who are tired, not a sale; calm would undersell it, hype would feel like a shout at a tired team) |
| Voice | Justin |
| Hook family | demonstration, Before and after (`before-after-on-screen`) |
| Flow pattern | one sentence, repeated, then collapsed (a before and after of a single task) |
| Design style | the studio's plainest one, big Inter type on the dark green night page; the type is the main actor (reasoning: no product UI exists, so type must carry it) |

**One sentence.** "They made typing the same answer a one-keystroke job."
**Feeling.** Relief.
**One idea.** The reply a support person has typed a hundred times, shown as it feels: the same sentence, over and over, until one keystroke turns the pile into a single reply.
**Signature moment (replayed).** Scene 3. The same sentence is stacked down the screen, line after line, each one a little dimmer. A slash appears, and the whole stack folds into one bright green chip that says "Refund policy". Quiet tick, no whoosh.
**Stage.** Dark green night page, bright green accent. Calm and low-lit like a late shift.
**Never.** 1. A made-up inbox screen presented as the real product. 2. People or hands (rule 23). 3. Words like "seamless" or "supercharge", or an opener like "Introducing".
**Different from the last five.** The ledger is empty, so there is nothing to repeat. Hook: a spoken accusation ("you just typed that again"). Look: type only, no UI. Move: repeat-and-collapse.
**New to the library.** `repeat-collapse`: a line of type stacked many times that folds into one element.
**References.** None chosen. The library holds no study card for this; stated, not invented.
**Facts that must be right.** "Saved replies" (exact name, said and written the same everywhere). "In the support inbox". Everything else is an example that needs a source (see Facts).

## Concept B: "Typed versus saved"

Hook family: comparison, Head to head (`head-to-head`). Flow: split screen race over the same ten tickets.
Idea: two columns of the same tickets, one answered by hand, one with saved replies. The right column finishes while the left is still typing.
Signature: the right column's progress bar hits done and the left stops mid-word.
Energy: hype. Design style: split-stage, light page against dark page.
Why not first: a race needs real timings, and no product exists to time. The film would be built on a number we could not measure. Risk: the trap in the hook library, a comparison with no honest ending.

## Concept C: "Not your typing speed"

Hook family: callout, Audience then reason (`audience-reason-not`). Flow: reframe (pain, reframe, promise).
Idea: replies feel slow because finding the words is the slow part, not typing. A shelf of answers appears where the hunting used to be.
Signature: a search for "that old ticket" loses itself in a pile, and a single slash replaces it.
Energy: calm. Design style: warm light page, quiet.
Why not first: argues against a belief nobody has told us the viewers hold, and the claim (finding is slower than typing) needs a source we do not have.

## Recommendation: A

It proves the claim with something the viewer sees, not a number we cannot source; it needs no invented screen; it opens with the feeling in the first three seconds; it is the easiest to make well in type alone.

## Facts (to confirm before the storyboard)

| Fact | Source |
|---|---|
| Feature name: "Saved replies" | Your brief |
| Lives in the support inbox | Your brief |
| Opened with a slash, and a name or a line can be edited before sending | Assumed from common practice; NOT confirmed for this product. Needs your yes, or a correction |
| Availability date, price, plans | Not given. Not claimed in the film |

## Storyboard note (for later, not a decision now)

Rule 10 says real UI only. The demo brand has no product, so scenes 3 and 4 cannot show a real saved-replies screen. Options at the storyboard: (a) you give a real capture or demo account; (b) the film shows the idea as drawn type and a clearly simple graphic, which you approve as such; (c) keep those scenes to type only. Default if you say nothing: (c).
EOF

result:
The idea is recorded as approved and the script and scene list are written. I've stopped at the script approval. I generated and played no audio, so nobody has heard the voice and I can't say how it sounds.

**Idea (recommended concept A, "Again")**
- The hook is "You just typed that same reply again." The same sentence stacks down the screen, then one slash folds the pile into a single green "Refund policy" chip. That fold is the signature moment.
- It is big white type on the dark green page, with a confident energy.
- I rejected concept B (typed vs saved race) because it needs timings we can't measure. I rejected concept C (not your typing speed) because it needs a claim we can't source.

**Script (Justin, the only voice on the demo brand)**

| # | Beat | Line |
|---|---|---|
| 01 | Hook | You just typed that same reply again. |
| 02 | Turn | Your best answer already exists. |
| 03 | Proof | With saved replies, you write an answer once. |
| 04 | Proof | Type a slash, pick it, and it's in the thread. |
| 05 | Proof | Change the name, tweak a line, and send. |
| 06 | Peak | Same answer, less typing. |
| 07 | Offer | Saved replies. Now in your support inbox. |
| 08 | Close | Write it once. |

**Five scenes:** S1 hook, S2 turn, S3 proof, S4 peak and offer, S5 close with a silent logo end card. The estimate is about 26.7 s of voice plus a roughly 3 s end card, so about 29.7 s against the 30 s cap.

**Checks:** the beat sheet passes except two flags I left in. The close reads short because the end card isn't counted yet. The line before the peak sits at energy 2, as the check asked, but the beat before it is still reported at 3. The word counts are estimates at 2.5 words a second, and the hook scores (7/8 for A) are my own judgement.

**Needs your answer or confirmation**
1. **No real screen exists.** The demo brand has no product, and the rule is real UI only, so I can't show a saved-replies screen. The scenes are type only unless you supply a real capture or approve a drawn graphic.
2. **Assumed behaviour.** I assumed a slash opens a reply and you can edit it before sending. You didn't tell me that. Please confirm or correct it.
3. **Voice.** The demo brand has no written voice. I wrote plain and warm, to one support person. Please correct it if that's wrong.
4. **Not claimed.** I gave no date, price or plan, because you didn't give any.

I recorded the idea gate with `gate.mjs approve`. The script and voice gate is still open.
